states.say: Dorian the Seer carried the Scrolls of Byzantem west. I can give you a map, a horse, and shelter; the road and its dangers remain yours to judge.

transitions.text: Ask what the crown expects in return.
Ask what the map can tell us.
Thank the king and leave.

states.say: Bring back knowledge that may aid Alsperia. I ask for no conquest, and I will not pretend a royal seal can make the western road safe.

transitions.text: I will remember your trust.

states.say: The map marks the road through Mistwood toward Lorian. It cannot tell us whether Dorian's old waystones still stand or what the scrolls contain.

transitions.text: Then we will verify the route as we travel.

states.say: Edmon is my husband and Alsperia's original king. His trust opens this road; what you learn about the scrolls will carry obligations beyond this court.

transitions.text: Ask what obligation she means.
Ask what she knows of the western road.
I will honor the trust you place in me.

states.say: Power can travel farther than the person who claims it. Keep a record of what the scrolls show, and of what they do not show, so the court cannot mistake a guess for knowledge.

transitions.text: I will keep the evidence distinct.

states.say: The court records name Mistwood and Lorian, but an old route is not a promise about the road today. Ask the people who live along it what has changed.

transitions.text: We will listen as we go.

states.say: I work on the magic knights’ armaments and on Alsperia’s magical craft. Neither discipline tells me what waits in Eldrador.

transitions.text: Ask how his work relates to this voyage.
Return to the charts.

states.say: You carry Selene’s marked account and Aven chose observation. Keep the incomplete record apart from the instruments; neither tells us what waits there.

transitions.text: Ask whether the preparations explain the Tear.
Keep the records distinct and proceed.

states.say: The marked account travels separately while Aven prepares a guarded arrival. Those preparations protect the inquiry; they do not settle the record.

states.say: Ealdrin carries Selene’s witness notes, and Aven chose observation. We can listen first without treating a witness account as a verdict.

states.say: The Aethercraft carries our instruments and records. My work on the magic knights’ armaments cannot tell us what the Eldrador Tear is.

states.say: I develop weapons and projectiles for Alsperia’s magic knights, and I am involved with the Aethercraft. I can describe our work, but it gives me no special knowledge of the Tear.

transitions.text: Thank you, Alistair.

states.say: No. The ship and its instruments prepare us to observe and protect the expedition; they cannot establish the Tear’s origin or meaning.
